title: Back-rank mates for either side
outcomes: Finds the back-rank mate for either side when no theme is named
Spots when his own back rank is the weakness by asking what the opponent's rook could check with
Says 'no threat' when a guard or a flight square removes the mate

steps.text: You know the pattern from **Back-rank mate, and luft as the cure**. Now it has to work for both sides, with nobody naming it. Before each move ask two questions. Can I check on the enemy first rank, and is that mate? Could the opponent do it to me: does my king have a free square, and does a piece of mine guard my first rank? Look at both kings, every time.

steps.caption: White to move. What does Black threaten, and how can White answer?

line.say: White makes a luft with the h-pawn, so the king gets the square h2.
Black checks on the first rank.
The king steps out. It was only a check.

claims.statement: If White passed, ...Re1 would be checkmate.

steps.text: A back-rank mate needs three things together: **no flight square**, **nothing that can capture the checking piece**, and **nothing that can block**. For your own king the same list is a checklist: one guard on the first rank, or one free square, removes the threat. As a **rule of thumb**, make air once a threat appears rather than on every move, because it costs a move and loosens the pawns. Predict before you look.

steps.title: Is there a threat to the black king?
steps.prompt: Only one feature changes each time. Predict whether White threatens mate.
Think of the position where you were slowest. Which king did you look at first, and did you check the other king's escape square? Which one did you skip? Rate your confidence (low / medium / high).
